paper.title: Fine-Grained Vehicle Make and Model Recognition Framework Based on Magnetic Fingerprint

evidence.paraphrase: Proposes fine-grained vehicle make and model recognition over 36 models for traffic perception.
Uses magnetic-sensor fingerprints instead of surveillance video, motivated by vision failures in low-visibility scenes.
Sensor modality differs from the video-based target task, so it bounds the task rather than sharing its method.

reviews.rationale: The paper is a fine-grained VMMR study and fits vehicle_make_model_scope, which is defined around the task and its evaluation boundary. Its non-visual modality makes it contrastive context, but the group assignment is sound and the group's omission from 27/150 bags is a genuine loss of task-bounding evidence.

paper.title: RESEARCH ON MULTI-OBJECT TRACKING OF PIGS BASED ON IMPROVED BYTE TRACK

evidence.paraphrase: Tracks pigs on livestock farms with YOLOv8 and an improved ByteTrack plus EMA trajectory smoothing.
Addresses trajectory interruption under frequent occlusion and reports MOTA/IDF1, which only analogises the vehicle detection-tracking pipeline group.
No vehicles, surveillance traffic scenes or recognition task appear in the abstract.

reviews.rationale: The paper is generic multi-object tracking in an animal-farming domain; its overlap with the vehicle pipeline group is limited to occlusion-robust tracking vocabulary. It is out of scope for vehicle make recognition, and its frequent selection where the target group was absent points to a lexical/semantic attraction rather than a valid substitute.

paper.title: Vehicle Classification Algorithm Based on Improved Vision Transformer

evidence.paraphrase: Adds a CNN branch for local features and a sparse attention module that screens discriminative regions to separate similar vehicles.
Task is vehicle type classification (BIT-Vehicles) plus generic image datasets, not make recognition.
No semantic vehicle parts or occlusion handling are described.

reviews.rationale: Local-region attention for discriminating similar vehicles is an analogue of part-based evidence, but the paper neither names semantic parts nor addresses occlusion or missing views. It is a partial analogue for semantic_parts_occlusion; as the group's most-explored candidate, its weak fit indicates limited direct coverage in the pool.

paper.title: Exploring Multi-Modal Spatial–Temporal Contexts for High-Performance RGB-T Tracking

evidence.paraphrase: Proposes a transformer network for generic RGB-thermal single-object tracking evaluated on RGB-T tracking benchmarks.
A quality-aware decoder propagates cues from historical frames, which resembles quality-aware temporal aggregation.
The temporal propagation serves target localisation, not accumulation of recognition evidence, and vehicles are not mentioned.

reviews.rationale: Temporal propagation in the tracker is a methodological analogue of quality-aware temporal fusion, but the task is object localisation in RGB-T video rather than recognising vehicle make from accumulated evidence. It is out of scope and a semantic false match, consistent with its use as a boundary example.
